### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/manifest.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via ERROR_CODE_LEDGER (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/manifest.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ee230a2516151ce1e754eb8146d6ea72af24826d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `003bb4db54a5bbc183560ae333a5428057565607` — the merge of head `631b9df53d9db40625a8d5b3f48ba88ec4f58471` into base `ee230a2516151ce1e754eb8146d6ea72af24826d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 003bb4db54a5bbc183560ae333a5428057565607 && git checkout 003bb4db54a5bbc183560ae333a5428057565607
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ee230a2516151ce1e754eb8146d6ea72af24826d 631b9df53d9db40625a8d5b3f48ba88ec4f58471 && git checkout -B drift-repro ee230a2516151ce1e754eb8146d6ea72af24826d && git merge --no-ff 631b9df53d9db40625a8d5b3f48ba88ec4f58471

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ee230a2516151ce1e754eb8146d6ea72af24826d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ee230a2516151ce1e754eb8146d6ea72af24826d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

  · PR #32792: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `631b9df53d9db40625a8d5b3f48ba88ec4f58471`
  · the check-runs on `631b9df53d9db40625a8d5b3f48ba88ec4f58471`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts

  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code

  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/77b29f66-4ec9-5f08-bb09-fd95702aafdf/scratchpad/issue-32586/pr-32792/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `631b9df53d9db40625a8d5b3f48ba88ec4f58471`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.module-package-second-app-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + packages/spec/liveness/manifest.json (the `manifest.type` evidence row that quotes `validateSingleApp`)

Inputs read: card #32586 body and its 7 comments; PR #32792 body, file list (7 files) and the net diff against `main` (`ee230a25`) at this head; the 67 check-runs on this head (every one `success` or `skipped`, none failed, none pending). Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: ADR-0019 D3 as amended, `defineStack` and `composeStacks` in `stack.zod.ts`, `migrations/types.ts`, `metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-scope.ts`, and the cli consumers of the finding text. The remainder of the diff (the changeset, `stack.test.ts`, `stack-duplicate-entry.test.ts`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `defineStack`, strict mode, `manifest.type: 'module'`, two or more `apps`: accepted before, refused now.** Right. It is the narrowing the card orders and the amended D3 states ("Read per package: no package of a suite defines more than one app"). `validateSingleApp` has one caller (`stack.zod.ts:6897`), so the narrowing lands at `defineStack` and nowhere else.
- **`type: 'app'`: accept set unchanged.** Right. Two or more apps were refused and still are; zero or one passes. Only the finding text changes.
- **Every other package type, a stack with no manifest, `strict: false`: unchanged.** Right. `type === undefined || !SINGLE_APP_PACKAGE_TYPES.has(type)` returns `[]` for all of them, and the check sits on the strict path only.
- **The narrowing also reaches a re-wrapped flat composition.** `defineStack(composeStacks([...]))` whose selected manifest (default `'last'`) is a module and whose concatenated `apps` holds two or more was accepted and is now refused. Right: that value is one package id carrying several apps, which is reason 1's broken shape, and the changeset's "a stack whose `manifest.type` is `'module'`" covers it literally. No production door re-runs `defineStack` on a composed artifact (`os compile` parses with the schema), so this arm is reachable only where an author writes the re-wrap.
- **`composeStacks` itself: accept set unchanged.** Right for this card (the claim's file surface excludes it), and it leaves the gap named in ③.
- **Refusal envelope: unchanged.** Code `STACK_SINGLE_APP_VIOLATION`, status 422, header `defineStack single-app validation failed`, one finding in `issues`. No new error code; the ledger enum and the generated JSON schemas do not move.
- **Finding text: changed for both types.** It now names the package id, quotes each app name, and cites "D3 as amended". The substring `must define at most one app` is kept, which is what `packages/cli/test/generate-scaffolds-reach-stack.e2e.test.ts:159` and `stack-refusal-envelopes.test.ts:134` match. Right; a message is not an accept set.
- **One new ADR-0087 semantic entry, `module-package-second-app-refused`, step 18, no D2 conversion.** Right. Which app stays is not derivable, so there is nothing mechanical to convert.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/32586-module-package-single-app.md` declares `@objectstack/spec` minor, with a BREAKING banner, a Before/Now/Unchanged/Fix body and the `adr-0087: registered module-package-second-app-refused` marker. A refused-where-accepted change in `defineStack` is a narrowing of a published accept set; this repository carries a narrowing as a minor with the narrowing declaration and a registered semantic entry, and `Check Changeset` and `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` are green on this head. The level matches what the diff publishes.

Clause-②: no (narrowing). The line is present and identical on the PR body and at the head of the changeset, with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` beside it on both. Correct: nothing is widened, one accepted shape is taken away, and that is what puts this PR at this tier.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Flat `composeStacks` (default `manifest: 'last'`) of an app package and module packages with one app each yields one package id with several apps, and nothing refuses it** (card comment 6818884972, first bullet; PR body shape 1). Confirmed by reading `composeStacks`: it concatenates `apps`, selects one manifest and never calls `validateSingleApp`. Leaving it out is correct for this card, since the claim excludes `composeStacks`. It is not answered, though: the PR body says "reported to the seat" and names no card. Escalated to the seat: a follow-up card is owed, because once this PR lands ADR-0019's status line will read as enforced while the default composition path still produces the removed shape. See nit N3, which touches the same gap from the author's side.
- **A `type: 'plugin'` package with two apps passes** (same comment, second bullet; PR body shape 2). Leaving it unjudged agrees with the amended D3, which defines a suite as an app package plus module packages. Whether plugins are held to one app is not decided by any ruling in the inputs. Escalated to the seat as an undecided question, not a defect of this diff.
- **A module body with two apps inside a hand-built `packages[]` passes `defineStack`** (PR body shape 3). Answered: on the authored route every body is itself the output of its own `defineStack` call and is judged there; only a hand-assembled artifact skips it. Same follow-up card as the first flag.
- **Cloud repository not measured** (card work item 2 and its acceptance line). The PR body states it plainly: no read access. This review cannot answer it either. Escalated to the seat: a seat with access measures it, or the PM accepts the risk in writing, before the card closes. A hit there would fail loudly at build with a remedy, not silently.
- **`Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md`.** Confirmed: line 141 of that file on this tree says `defineStack` refuses a second app "in a `type: 'app'` package", which becomes narrow, not false. Card comment 6821116381 asked the landing PR to name a `domain:skills` sub-card; the body names the file and no card. The seat owes the card number at ACCEPT.
- **Records outside the diff that this change makes stale, not named in the PR body.** ADR-0019's status line ("Pending: the `defineStack` check that holds a module package to at most one app") and its "Enforced today, and not yet" paragraph; ADR-0130's fact row "`validateSingleApp` constrains only `type: 'app'`" (line 154). Both are dated readings and both are governed text a product PR does not edit. Follow-up owed with the Tier H route; not a finding on this diff.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay note is owed.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`** — holds against the amended D3 and against its first consumers.

- `SINGLE_APP_PACKAGE_TYPES` (line 2611) is `app` and `module`, exactly the two package types the amendment's rule and terminology table build a suite from. Its docblock's three reasons restate the amendment's three, each accurately, including the qualifier on reason 2 ("where its own package defines objects").
- `validateSingleApp` (lines 2630 to 2643), sentence by sentence against its docblock: judges only the set's types (true); more than one app is refused (true, `apps.length` over 1); the finding names the package, every app and the remedy (true); an app package is also offered the fold (true); zero apps allowed (true); one error per violation (true).
- The card's acceptance scenario holds: a module with two apps is refused naming both; HotCRM's planned shape (one app in each of the app, service and marketing packages, composed under `preserve`) is untouched, because each input is judged alone by its own `defineStack` and `composeStacks` does not run this check.
- Attempts to break it: map-form `apps` (normalized to an array before the check, names intact); an absent manifest (not judged, as before); a multi-package `preserve` artifact fed back through `defineStack` (the flat `apps` copy is normally stripped, so it passes; where the copy is kept, the result is the re-wrap case judged right in ①); validation order (unchanged, after the namespace check). None produced a wrong refusal or a wrong acceptance inside the card's scope.
- The server-side reader agrees with the rule as now enforced: `protocol-package-scope.ts` answers a package-id app read as absent when the package holds more than one app, for any package type.
- `StackSingleAppViolationError` docblock (line 3737): agrees with the code.

Findings on this file:

- **N1 (nit)** — lines 2621 to 2623 and 2636: the module finding withholds the fold remedy, and the docblock says "an app package may instead fold", which reads as if a module may not. The semantic entry's `replacement` and the changeset both offer the fold to a module. Folding a module's apps into one is plainly valid, so the three texts disagree on guidance only. No effect on what is accepted.
- **N2 (nit)** — line 2635: `kind` hard-codes two labels beside a set. A third type added to `SINGLE_APP_PACKAGE_TYPES` would be reported as "A 'module' package". Deriving the label from `type` would keep the message true by construction. No effect today.
- **N3 (nit)** — lines 2639 to 2642: the finding tells the author to move each other app into a module of its own and does not say the packages must be composed under `manifest: 'preserve'`. The semantic entry and the changeset do say it. An author who follows the finding and composes with the default gets one package id with several apps and no refusal (the first flag in ③). Guidance only; the hole itself is outside this card.

**`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.module-package-second-app-refused.ts`** — holds against ADR-0087's entry type and the ruling it implements.

- All four required fields of `SemanticMigration` are present; the id matches the changeset marker; `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` is green.
- `surface` names the narrowed shape exactly. `reason` restates the amendment's three reasons, each checked against the ADR text and, for the package-id read, against `protocol-package-scope.ts`. "Not convertible" is right. `replacement` is the correct remedy and names `preserve`. `acceptanceCriteria` is checkable by the consumer.
- No `conversionIds`: right, no D2 conversion exists.
- **N4 (nit)** — no `relevantWhen`. The surface lives under `apps` (top level or in a package body), so the entry is listed for every consumer of the step, including stacks with no app at all. Omitting it is the safe default the type documents, so this is an accepted deviation, not a defect.

**`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`** — line 1849, a comment only. It now says what the code refuses and cites the amendment. The enum member, its family and its status are untouched. Holds.

**`packages/spec/liveness/manifest.json`** (implementing file) — the rewritten evidence quotes `const type = config.manifest?.type`, which is the read at `stack.zod.ts:2631`, and its gloss names the set and both types. The anchor `stack.zod.ts#validateSingleApp` still resolves, and `Spec property liveness` is green. Agrees with the code.

No must-fix and no should-fix. Four nits; each is left as an accepted deviation or goes to a follow-up card, since a fix in `stack.zod.ts` or the entry moves the head and this record would no longer cover it.
